statement: A curve is given parametrically by $x=t^{2}$, $y=t^{3}$. (i) Find $\\frac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$. (ii) Find the equation of the normal at the point where $t=1$. (iii) Find where this normal meets the $x$-axis.
solution: (i) $dx/dt=2t$, $dy/dt=3t^{2}$, so $dy/dx=3t^{2}/(2t)=3t/2$. (ii) At $t=1$ the point is $(1,1)$ and the tangent slope is $3/2$, so the normal slope is $-2/3$: $y-1=-\\frac{2}{3}(x-1)$. (iii) Set $y=0$: $-1=-\\frac{2}{3}(x-1)\\Rightarrow x-1=3/2\\Rightarrow x=5/2$.
hints: The normal slope is the negative reciprocal.
